note: Reel 15: Google Lost $475 Billion in a Day. Alphabet's stock fell 12.6% on 29 Oct 2026 after its Q3 results: about $475 billion of market value, the second-biggest one-day loss for a US-listed company (only Nvidia, ~$593 billion in Jan 2025, lost more; Yahoo Finance/Bloomberg). The paradox: sales +25%, Cloud +103%. The why: Search & other is half of revenue ($63.4B of $127.6B); AI Mode queries grow, and Google said AI Mode monetizes lower (Philipp Schindler on the call); capex $51.4B in Q3 (~$558M a day); free cash flow negative two quarters running (Q2 -$5.9B, Q3 -$9.1B). The ending: not broke ($265B in cash and securities), but is Google's AI eating Google? Facts and sources: docs/research.md. Kokoro af_heart, speed 1.0 (memory: narration pace). Numbers as words. 'data centres' is spelt 'centers' for the American voice (text_kokoro).

lines.text: Google just lost four hundred and seventy-five billion dollars. In one day.
Only Nvidia has ever lost more.
Strange, because Google's sales had just grown twenty-five percent.
Its cloud business more than doubled.
The answer is in your search bar. Half of Google's money comes from search ads.
But more searches now happen in AI Mode, where Google's AI just answers you.
And Google admitted AI Mode earns less.
Then there's the bill: fifty-one billion dollars in three months, on AI data centres.
lines.text_kokoro: Then there's the bill: fifty-one billion dollars in three months, on AI data centers.

lines.text: Over half a billion dollars a day.
Two quarters in a row, Google spent more cash than it brought in.
It's paying for the very AI that's eating into its search ads.
But Wall Street now has one question: is Google's AI eating Google?
